text.p: All Nippon Airways Co Ltd (ANA), has increased its Italy-Japan flights to five a week, an ANA spokesman said.

Speaking at a press conference held for the launch of ANA services from Malpensa Milan Airport to Osaka, Wataru Kubo, ANA senior vice president and general manager Europe, said flights from Rome to Osaka had increased their frequency from twice to five times a week.
One of the three new flights stops over at Milan and the other two route via Frankfurt. The first Milan flight took off on September 9.
ANA launched the Rome-Osaka route in December 1995, since that time it has handled nearly 30,000 passengers and 373 tonnes of freight.

Kubo said: "This is our tenth European route and the fifth European point we serve. With the opening of the Milan connection and the strengthening of our position in Rome we now have a 30 percent share of the market between Italy and Japan and we aim to better this position."
The Milan-Osaka flight is operated with a Boeing 747-200 every Monday.
Kubo added:"We now have 50 flights a week between Europe and Japan amounting to a 13 percent share of the traffic on the route."
Meanwhile, Toru Suzuki, general manager of ANA's Rome office has been named the new manager of its Milan office as well, a company statement said.
Previously Suzuki was ANA station manager at London Heathrow Airport.
